title: Strategies for LLM Evals (GuideLLM, lm-eval-harness, OpenAI Evals Workshop) — Taylor Jordan Smith
talk_summary: The talk argues production LLM systems need layered evaluations, not just benchmarks, and demonstrates GuideLLM for latency/throughput, lm-eval-harness/MMLU Pro for accuracy, and promptfoo for custom safety/bias evals. It recommends starting with component-level evals and wiring them into CI/CD like software tests.

takeaways.what_they_do: Build evals incrementally by layer: system performance, formatting, factual accuracy, safety/bias, then custom app-specific tests, mirroring unit/integration/end-to-end software testing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can take that layer by layer as you're building this evaluation framework for your systems.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run eval tests in CI/CD like unit tests, continuously improving them as part of the release process.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you should have a CI/CD framework that includes these evaluation tests just like for unit testing setups

takeaways.what_they_do: Use GuideLLM to sweep request rates and input/output token lengths matching chatbot/RAG/agent use cases; measure TTFT, inter-token latency, throughput, and P99.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can adjust the um input and output token levels based on your use case.
takeaways.numbers: GuideLLM run at rate 5; L4 GPU; 2B/8B model; reports mean/median/P99

takeaways.evidence_quote: you can do all kinds of custom tests with prompt fu
you can just like fork it and ch and change the data sources.
